public_rationale: The September survey shows that high and volatile costs prompted workload changes. That is relevant to Zitron's explanation, but it does not establish broad cuts in realized AI spending. The comparison with all other organizational costs also remains unverified. No decisive event resolves this undated forecast.
limitations: The strongest recent evidence is a vendor-commissioned survey of deployment decisions.
The claim does not distinguish project cuts from total expenditure cuts.
Unknown accounting basis prevents a supported or contradicted monetary assessment.

statement.excerpt: The reason I’m so confident AI gets cut is that its cost is volatile due to the nature of LLMs and harnesses and prompts and all the other bits that go into making them do something, and are so much higher than anything else in an organization.

from_speaker: due to the nature of LLMs and harnesses and prompts

our_interpretation: Read as a forecast of broad, material enterprise AI spending reductions caused by high and variable costs.
Confidence is not a conditional antecedent.
Cuts to individual deployments are relevant but do not by themselves establish a broad reduction in total AI spending.
The comparison with everything else in an organization is retained as an unverified premise; it is not silently narrowed to software costs.
criteria.support_condition: Representative expenditure records show material enterprise AI spending reductions, and decision records attribute them to unusually high and volatile costs.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence decisively establishes a completed broad retrenchment whose causes exclude the stated cost mechanism. Continued growth alone does not refute an undated prediction of eventual cuts.
